ai.description: Doria’s Asian Treefrog (Rhacophoridae) is a small frog reaching 30–35 mm. It is brownish-tan with a dark, triangular interorbital mark and distinct, enlarged adhesive discs on all digits.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Chirixalus doriae* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark-edged light stripe running along the side of its head and body, which is absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: Doria's Asian treefrog inhabits moist evergreen and semi-evergreen forests, typically found among low-lying vegetation near water bodies at mid-to-high altitudes.
ai.behavior: Doria's Asian treefrog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects among the vegetation near forest pools and streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Chirixalus doriae* breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs enclosed in foam nests attached to vegetation overhanging water bodies.
ai.distributionRemarks: Doria's Asian treefrog occurs in Northeast India, specifically in Assam and Arunachal Pradesh, typically inhabiting mid-elevation forests in the Himalayan foothills.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Chirixalus doriae* consists of a series of short, high-pitched, insect-like chirps, typically heard from vegetation near forest pools.
